title: Opportunistic Kernel Switching — experiment notes
content:
Purpose:
Short: iterate on a low-risk runtime mechanism that switches attention kernel implementations at request time to reduce p99/p999 tail latency without regressing median throughput.

Motivation / hypothesis:
- We see occasional long tails for mid-length chat requests (seq_len 512–1536) in mixed workloads.
- Hypothesis A: Some kernels (Flash-backed fused kernels) are excellent for long single-shot generations but suffer sporadic latency spikes when co-scheduled with many small-batch requests due to buffer thrash and scheduler preemption.
- Hypothesis B: Paged-attention (KV-paged) kernels handle heterogeneous prefix-heavy workloads more gracefully but cost more average GPU cycles for very short completions.
- Idea: Implement an opportunistic kernel switcher in the runtime that selects an attention kernel variant per-request based on cheap heuristics (prefix length, estimated output length, client latency SLO, current queue depth, and recent per-kernel staleness signals). The switcher falls back to a safe kernel on error.

Experiment goals:
- Measure p50 / p95 / p99 / p999 token latency impact of opportunistic switching vs always-Flash vs always-paged.
- Track cost (GPU utilization, tokens/sec), correctness (numerical diffs within tolerance), and failure modes (kernel fallback frequency, OOMs).
- Verify no throughput regression for steady-state traffic and acceptable overhead on per-request decision path (<200us added).

Setup (hardware/software):
- Cluster: 8x A100-80GB in a single availability zone.
- Serving runtime: branch feature/opportunistic-kernels (runtime v0.23.1 + local patch).
- Models: 13B causal transformer, quantized to q4f16 wherever applicable.
- Test harness: workload-replayer (modified) that replays observed production traces (mix of short chat, long context, embeddings).
- Traces used: prod-trace-2025-01-06 (anonymized).

Switch decision heuristics (prototype):
- If request.client_slo == "low" (<=100ms) and prompt_len < 64: prefer small-batch optimized kernel (tiny-fused).
- If prefix_tokens > 384 or context_kv_size_estimate > 40MB: prefer paged-kv path to avoid large KV cache snapshots.
- If queue_depth > 16 and average_batch_size < 4: prefer small-batch kernel to reduce scheduler blocking.
- Otherwise: default to Flash-fused kernel.

Implementation notes (runtime changes):
- Decision is pure heuristic implemented as a single function called before dispatch. Kept side-effect free to avoid RB-state coupling. Added a lightweight per-worker ring buffer of last 128 decisions to collect statistics.
- Kernel switch requires compatible configuration: same model sharding layout and quantization profile. We reject switch if incompatible and fall back to default safe kernel.
- Added observability: per-request label kernel_variant and decision_reason; aggregate dashboards keyed by model_id + kernel_variant.

Microbench commands used:
- Local microbench (single GPU, isolated):
  - run_microbench --model 13B --kernel flash --batch-size 1 --seq 768 --iters 2000
  - run_microbench --model 13B --kernel paged --batch-size 1 --seq 768 --iters 2000
- Cluster replay (multi-worker):
  - workload-replayer --trace prod-trace-2025-01-06 --mode parallel24 --switcher feature_flag_on
- Extraction of tail histograms:
  - ./bin/latency-agg --input replay-output.jsonl --percentiles 50,95,99,999 --group-by kernel_variant

Representative raw results (single-run summaries):
- Baseline (always-Flash): p50=7.2ms, p95=34ms, p99=128ms, p999=420ms, tokens/s=22k, GPU util=76%
- Baseline (always-paged): p50=8.9ms, p95=42ms, p99=82ms, p999=210ms, tokens/s=18.5k, GPU util=68%
- Opportunistic switcher (heuristic): p50=7.5ms, p95=36ms, p99=60ms, p999=140ms, tokens/s=20.6k, GPU util=72%
  - Notes: p99 and p999 improved significantly vs always-Flash, median close to baseline. Throughput dropped ~6% vs Flash baseline but improved vs paged baseline.

Deeper observations:
- The biggest wins at the tail come from routing long-prefix requests (historical chat) to paged-kv, which avoided large contiguous KV memory copies that occasionally triggered kernel stalls in the Flash path.
- Many p999 events in the Flash baseline coincided with model migrations (hot resharding) and GC events. Opportunistic approach avoided some of those by steering around vulnerable kernel combos.
- The decision overhead measured at ~120–160us median in our current Go runtime; small but measuring inlined hotpaths should be considered.
- Numeric diffs between kernels were small (<1e-4 average L2 on logits) when quantization equivalent; pass rate 99.98% for exact match tolerance on sampled tokens. Some mismatch on beam search tie-breaking — need canonical post-processing agreement.

Failure modes and incidents:
- 2024-12-12 run: observed a 0.3% increase in soft OOMs when switching frequently under bursty traffic. Root cause: paged-kv reservation logic didn't respect transient prefetch reservation; fixed by deferring large page reservations until after steady-state chunking window.
- Some legacy models have hand-optimized kernels that are incompatible with runtime switch; we detect and force the legacy kernel (decision_reason=legacy_incompatible).

Open questions / next experiments:
- Can we learn the switching policy? Quick offline RL approach: treat kernel choice as action, reward = negative tail latency + alpha * tokens/s. Use logged bandit approach (IPS) with existing traces.
- How does switching behavior interact with autoscaling? If we route many long-prefix requests to paged path, server-side memory pressure might trigger scale-up earlier; need to simulate cluster-level capacity planning.
- Is there an I/O amplification or PCIe thrash pattern when mixing kernel types? We should add perf counters for NVLink/PCIe and track copy sizes.
- Should the decision be client-visible (SDK hint)? Expose kernel_preference in API so advanced clients can opt in.

Immediate action items:
- [ ] Add NVLink / PCIe copy metric to the profiling agent (Ravi)
- [ ] Run a week-long A/B against a small subset of prod traffic (2% users) with logging-only decision to collect labels for offline learning (Jordan)
- [ ] Implement safe-rate-limiter for switch frequency to avoid oscillation (Ellen)
- [ ] Draft API changes for kernel_preference flag and review with API team (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Re-run numeric diff suite adding beam-search canonicalization tests (owner: Maya/Jordan)

Appendix: sample log line (prototype)
2025-01-12T14:03:21.832Z model=13B req=abc123 kernel_variant=paged decision_reason=long_prefix(prefix=512) decision_latency_us=143 gpu_util=0.71 p99_hist_bucket=120ms

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep heuristics conservative; prefer paged only when we have a clear memory/copy reason.
- We should avoid adding too many variants — maintenance cost grows combinatorially with kernels * quant profiles.
- Consider a lightweight feature store (per-model) to tune thresholds derived from real telemetry rather than hard-coded constants.

End of notes.
